comments.author: banach-space
comments.body:
Thanks for reporting! Could you share a reproducer and let us know which project is this commit from? 

> This test was enabled by recent commit 82c07c75

comments.author: omjavaid
comments.body:
This is from [llvm-test-suite](https://github.com/llvm/llvm-test-suite) gfortran tests. I pushed a commit 4049776b to disable this tests. It fails on following LLVM buildbots

https://lab.llvm.org/buildbot/#/builders/198
https://lab.llvm.org/buildbot/#/builders/184
https://lab.llvm.org/buildbot/#/builders/197
https://lab.llvm.org/buildbot/#/builders/176

comments.author: banach-space
comments.body:
> I pushed a commit 4049776b to disable this tests.

Thanks! Would you mind sharing links to commits that you refer to? It's much easier if all the information is in one place :) 

Looking at one particular failure (https://lab.llvm.org/buildbot/#/builders/184/builds/9092/steps/13/logs/FAIL__test-suite__gfortran-regression-compile-regr):
```bash
> UNREACHABLE executed at ../llvm/llvm/lib/Target/AArch64/AArch64ISelLowering.cpp:6102!
```

Looks like a something specific to AArch64. Do we run these tests on any other platforms?

CC @klausler who pushed 82c07c75.

comments.author: omjavaid
comments.body: @banach-space i am not aware of all the commits from the LLVM side which should have fixed this test. @klausler might know better which Fortran features or bug fix should have fixed this tests.

comments.author: banach-space
comments.body:
> @banach-space i am not aware of all the commits from the LLVM side which should have fixed this test.

What I meant is sharing [82c07c75](https://github.com/llvm/llvm-test-suite/commit/82c07c75972330c43c4fb93a863fdbbc3f087873) instead of 82c07c75 ;-)

comments.author: Leporacanthicus
comments.body:
The underlying reason for the failure is the lack of trampolines in AArch64. The basic problem is passing arguments from an outer scope through to a function pointer.

I'll come back with some supporting material in a little bit.

comments.author: Leporacanthicus
comments.body:
This raises the issue:
https://github.com/JuliaLang/julia/issues/27174

There's an RFC about support for this here: https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/pull/66157
I pointed out the above bug in that review.

comments.author: Leporacanthicus
comments.body:
Although that is supposed to be fixed here: https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/pull/70267

So not entirely sure what the problem is...

comments.author: klausler
comments.body:
Tom Eccles gave me an all-clear for aarch64, so I don't know what went wrong there.  I should probably just stop upstreaming test enablements to llvm-test-suite.

What's left to be done for this bug?

comments.author: Leporacanthicus
comments.body:
> Tom Eccles gave me an all-clear for aarch64, so I don't know what went wrong there. I should probably just stop upstreaming test enablements to llvm-test-suite.

That's a bit extreme. You are certainly not the first, unlikely the last to do an "Oops, I broke something I couldn't test locally".
> 
> What's left to be done for this bug?

I first thought it was as easy as "it's not been implemented", but there seems to be code there to solve this. See PR mentioned above.

I haven't looked into the details, as I've got another important task to work on. The PR above says it should work on Linux, will not work on Windows or MacOS - but this is a Linux build, so shouldn't be a problem that it doesn't work on other OSes.

I may be able to take a look after I've got my current work sorted out (at least as far as trying to narrow down the underlying problem a bit more closely).

comments.author: ceseo
comments.body:
> Although that is supposed to be fixed here: #70267
> 
> So not entirely sure what the problem is...

My PR hasn't been merged yet. Someone else mentioned a while back on Phabricator that he would try another approach to solve this problem without relying on a compiler-rt dependency. I don't know the current status of that.

comments.body:
> > Although that is supposed to be fixed here: #70267
> > So not entirely sure what the problem is...
> 
> My PR hasn't been merged yet. Someone else mentioned a while back on Phabricator that he would try another approach to solve this problem without relying on a compiler-rt dependency. I don't know the current status of that.

Ah, that'll be why it still fails... :) Mystery solved. It helps if you actually can read the PR page correctly, and when you (as in I) see the "Squash and merge" don't accept that as "already merged".

@klausler I'm not sure if there's a way to enable the test for only some OS/Processor (e.g. x86 & Linux only) or not. Otherwise, I guess we have to wait until the above ticket is resolved...

comments.author: ceseo
comments.body: @Leporacanthicus my suggestion would be to approve this PR and I'd add a comment stating that, in the future, it would be better to remove the compiler-rt dependency, like X86 does.
